title: ECLSS alarm-threshold and survival-protocol audit for OTA-TEC-0019 (pCO2, pO2, leak rates, survival pressure)
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0019-2091-DE ECLSS survival SOP against primary aerospace-medicine, NASA/ESA ECLSS and human-physiology sources. Assess only the externally checkable physiology/engineering layer: (1) verify the CO2 (pCO2) alarm thresholds — NOMINAL < 0.4 kPa (~3 mmHg), GELB 0.4-0.9 kPa (~3-7 mmHg), ROT 0.9-2.0 kPa (~7-15 mmHg), SCHWARZ > 2.0 kPa (>15 mmHg) — against NASA spacecraft CO2 SMAC values, the ISS CO2 partial-pressure operating range, and acute hypercapnia / CO2-toxicity limits, including whether LiOH activation at 0.9 kPa is consistent with real spacecraft practice; (2) verify the O2 (pO2) thresholds (NOMINAL 18-21 kPa, GELB 17-18, ROT < 17, SCHWARZ < 15 kPa) against cabin-oxygen/hypoxia standards (equivalent altitude, time-of-useful-consciousness) and NASA/ESA habitable-pressure practice; (3) assess the cabin leak-rate thresholds (NOMINAL < 50 Pa/min, GELB 50-150, ROT 150-400, SCHWARZ > 400 Pa/min) against real spacecraft leak-detection/depressurization criteria and the depressurization times these rates imply for a KITE-class cabin volume; (4) verify the 'survival mode' pressure of 60-65 kPa (~0.6 atm) against hypobaric-tolerance, flammability, structural-load and EVA-prebreathing logic, and the '2 L/person/day' water-restriction figure; (5) check the stated emergency systems against real ECLSS/escape-system practice — LiOH-cartridge activation for CO2 spikes and the claimed regeneration of scrubber A/B, chlorate ('O2 candle') candles ignited singly at 30-60 s intervals with a thermal-load caveat, and fire-suppressor pre-verification; (6) identify wording in the thresholds that should be narrowed, corrected or reclassified [R]/[H]/[F], and which figures are defensible as realistic operational SOP values. Do NOT evaluate or alter the fictional KITE-class vehicle, the 2065-2100 applicability window, crew/capacity numbers, narrative canon, or any NOXIA/OTA balancing value.
why_now: OTA-TEC-0019 is a priority-12 operational SOP whose entire emergency architecture rests on concrete numeric thresholds (pCO2, pO2, leak rate, survival pressure). These are directly checkable against NASA SMAC, ISS operations and aerospace-medicine standards; any mismatch propagates into crew-safety framing across the KITE/ECLSS canon. No prior research has verified these specific anchors, and the document carries a relation_gap with the KITE specification it governs.
real_world_anchor: Real aerospace-medicine and ECLSS standards: NASA Spacecraft Maximum Allowable Concentrations for CO2, ISS pCO2/pO2 operational ranges, hypoxic and hypercapnic physiological limits, spacecraft cabin leak-rate and depressurization criteria, hypobaric survival pressure (0.6 atm), LiOH CO2 scrubbing, and chlorate-candle (O2 candle) oxygen-generation practice.
novelty_reason: RES-20260831-TEC0082B assessed general life-support requirements for the CYGNUS CTV (CO2 removal, consumables, fault tolerance) but did not verify this SOP's specific numeric alarm thresholds (pCO2/pO2 in kPa, leak rates in Pa/min, survival pressure 60-65 kPa, 2 L/person/day) against NASA SMAC and aerospace-medicine standards, nor its LiOH-regeneration and O2-candle operational claims.
